name: Rerovik
description: Rerovik is a precision SNT-active compound that targets habitual trigger-response pathways — the neural routes that fire when a user encounters environmental, social, or sensory cues associated with past drug use. By temporarily destabilizing these pathways during a 48-hour window of intensive behavioral therapy, Rerovik allows new associations to be written over old ones. It is always used in conjunction with a certified behavioral protocol; alone it produces only confusion.
effects: Reduced automatic craving response to environmental triggers
side_effects: Extreme suggestibility during active window — dangerous without controlled therapeutic environment
In uncontrolled settings: can be used to implant new triggers rather than remove old ones
duration: Active window 48 hours; pathway changes intended to be permanent
street_price: Φ2,400 per session (clinic); Φ600-900 for stolen doses without protocol
cultural_context: Rerovik sessions are considered cutting-edge recovery in Tier 3-4 facilities — a one-time intensive intervention that can break even years of deeply conditioned trigger responses. The extreme suggestibility during the window has made it controversial: there are documented cases of unethical practitioners using it to implant new behaviors rather than remove old ones. On the street, stolen doses are occasionally used recreationally for the plasticity window itself — people use them to try to rewrite other things about themselves, with unpredictable results.
story_hooks: Someone the players trust has undergone a Rerovik session and come out subtly different — not cleaner, just... different — and the therapeutic records have been sealed

A stolen Rerovik dose is on the market and someone desperate is going to use it alone, without protocol, because they can't afford the clinic — the players have to decide whether to stop them or help them do it safely
A Helix researcher has developed a modified Rerovik protocol that can target any habitual behavior, not just drug use — the applications are obvious and the ethics are catastrophic
